title: introduce-stream-sanitizer-heuristic-for-safe-split-merge-and-atomic-fncall-ordering
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see intermittent client-reported failures where an SSE stream contains a mid-JSON split combined with trailing delimiter runs that cause downstream OpenAI-compatible clients to surface 'unexpected end of JSON' or misassociate subsequent function/tool-call events. Previously we relied on conservative byte-boundary heuristics which either over-coalesced (increasing latency) or under-merged (producing partial JSON emissions). This PR introduces a small, deterministic 'stream sanitizer' pipeline stage that: 1) performs token-aware boundary estimation (approximate BPE/UTF-8 aware heuristic) to avoid splitting inside multi-byte or token-critical regions, 2) adds ephemeral span-anchor comments into the SSE stream to enable clients and proxies to resync boundaries after reconnects, and 3) rewrites ambiguous delimiter runs into a canonical delimiter form so downstream parsers see unambiguous event separators. The sanitizer is designed to be low-latency and opt-in for routes that require strict structured-output guarantees.
Checklist: - [x] Add stream sanitizer implementation in Go (server-side) - [x] Add compatibility adapter in Python layer for OpenAI-compatible SSE clients - [x] Add unit and integration tests covering UTF-8 multi-byte splits, backslash-escaped delimiters, and interleaved function-call sequencing - [x] Document behavior and opt-in config in streaming docs - [x] Run full CI and validate against existing stream stability benchmarks
High-level changes (commits summary): - 8a1e3b0: initial stream-sanitizer package and token-aware boundary estimator - b7c2f41: introduce span-anchor comment event generator and canonical delimiter normalizer - c3f9d22: openai_compat adapter: consume span-anchor comments and treat them as no-op for existing clients - d1e0a9a: add unit tests for partial-json repair scenarios and UTF-8 edge cases - ee4b5c8: integration tests: simulate reconnects and ensure fncall ordering preserved - f12a7b9: docs: streaming/sanitizer.md and configuration knobs - 7b9c0d4: perf tweaks and microbenchmarks for estimator (reduced overhead)
Files changed (high-level): - server/streaming/sanitizer/rewriter.go (new): core heuristic and rewrite pipeline - server/streaming/sanitizer/heuristic_test.go (new): unit tests for boundary heuristics - compat/openai/sse_adapter.py (modified): ignore :span-anchor: comments and treat canonical delimiters as single events - tests/integration/streams/test_reconnect_fncall_order.py (new): end-to-end reconnect + toolcall ordering scenarios - docs/streaming/sanitizer.md (new): operator-facing notes and opt-in config - build/ci/streaming/benchmark-config.yaml (modified): include sanitizer perf runs - CHANGELOG.md (modified): user-facing note
This PR keeps the sanitizer opt-in via route config: streaming.sanitizer.enabled = true, and provides a configurable threshold: streaming.sanitizer.token_lookahead = 24 (bytes) so we don't overrun CPU on extremely high QPS routes.
Implementation notes and rationale: - Token-aware estimator: we do not run a full tokenizer in the hot path. Instead we use a lightweight heuristic that combines UTF-8 rune safety (always avoid splitting in the middle of a multi-byte rune), a small lookbehind for escape/backslash sequences, and a rolling byte entropy check to approximate BPE token boundaries for common model vocabularies. This reduces false-positive splits without imposing heavy CPU cost.
- Span-anchor comment events: SSE supports comment lines (lines starting with ':'). We emit ephemeral comments of the form ":span-anchor:<hex-id>" at logical event boundaries when the sanitizer makes a non-trivial rewrite. These anchors are idempotent and ignored by existing clients (per SSE spec) but allow a reconnecting proxy or our OpenAI-compat adapter to resynchronize event reconstruction windows without relying on heavy checksum state. Anchors are strictly informational and have no bearing on model output semantics.
- Canonical delimiter normalization: some upstream proxies coalesce repeated delimiter sequences in different ways (\n\n, \r\n\r\n, mixed CR/LF). We normalize to a single \n\n sequence and ensure that function-call sentinel lines (data: {"tool": ...}) are preserved as atomic spans.
Testing summary: - Unit tests cover: UTF-8 split avoidance, escape-backslash edgecases, canonical delimiter rewriting, and token_lookahead boundary scenarios. - Integration tests added a simulated flaky connection that severs streams at mid-json; the receiver (compat adapter) successfully reconstructs JSONs using span-anchor metadata and canonical delimiters; function-call message ordering is preserved across reconnects and replay. - Added a small microbenchmark (server side) demonstrating median added latency of ~0.35ms per event under typical workloads with token_lookahead 24.
Review thread (high level): - Priya: "This addresses the onboarding ticket ENG-1122 and matches the spec we reviewed. Two nits: add a note in streaming.md about span-anchor visibility to customers and expand one test for long-running embeddings streams." - Asha (author): "Added docs note and extended test to cover long embedding sequences (see tests/integration/streams/test_reconnect_fncall_order.py)." - Daniel: "Concern: heuristic could cause extra CPU on Dedicated nodes at high QPS. Can we gate via per-route config and ensure the heuristic short-circuits on small payloads?" - Asha: "Heuristic short-circuits when event size < 128 bytes (configurable), and we added a route-level toggle. Updated perf numbers and added benchmark to CI." - Liam: "Please ensure OpenAI-compat adapter ignores anchors (we don't want SDKs to expose them). Also please add a short blurb to CHANGELOG about opt-in behavior." - Asha: "Adapter updated; anchors are emitted as comments and explicitly stripped by compat layer. CHANGELOG updated."
CI and rollout: - Initial CI run: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration/streams (fail on flaky reconnection test due to a race in test harness). - Rerun after test harness fix: all checks passed including integration/streams, lint/format checks, and streaming benchmarks within acceptable thresholds. - ci_status: pass
Merge outcome: - Merged to main via squash by Priya Shenoy on 2026-02-20. Merge commit message: "stream(sanitizer): add heuristic split/merge rewriter and span-anchor resync for partial-json robustness (ENG-1122)"
Release notes (for CHANGELOG and release manager): - Add opt-in stream sanitizer for routes requiring structured-output guarantees; default disabled. - Adds span-anchor comment markers for resynchronization (ignored by standard SSE clients). - Config knobs: streaming.sanitizer.enabled (bool), streaming.sanitizer.token_lookahead (int), streaming.sanitizer.min_event_bytes (int).
Backwards compatibility and risk: - Backwards compatible when disabled. - When enabled, we emit only SSE comment lines and canonicalize delimiters; existing clients per SSE spec will ignore comments and should not see behavioral changes except improved JSON reconstructions. - Operational risk: small CPU overhead when enabled; recommend enabling gradually on Dedicated or lower-QPS routes and monitoring streaming.latency.p50/p95 and cpu.util metrics.
Notes for on-call / SRE: - If unexpected failures occur after enabling, first toggle streaming.sanitizer.enabled=false for the route (route config can be changed via console or config API) then collect streaming debug logs (server/streaming/sanitizer logs have trace-level boundary events). - Anchors are safe to ignore; do not attempt to parse them as model payload.
Related work: - ENG-1133 (follow-up plan to add probabilistic checksum fallback if reconnects happen without anchors) - Docs: streaming/sanitizer.md includes a developer-facing example for enabling the sanitizer on a route and troubleshooting guidance.
release_notes: Add opt-in stream sanitizer (disabled by default); span-anchor comments for resync; config knobs: streaming.sanitizer.enabled, token_lookahead, min_event_bytes
